dimension_grades.evidence: The dependency upgrade false lead is mentioned in a single sentence ('I spent some time looking through changelogs but didn't find anything suspicious') with no detail about what was investigated or why it seemed plausible.

The author never takes personal ownership of the mistake; the closest is a passive observation that 'This cache was added in a quick PR that didn't get thorough review,' with no indication the author wrote it or approved it.
No specific time durations are given for wrong paths; the only hint is 'took us a while to figure out,' which is vague and does not make the cost felt.
The tone throughout is neutral and instructional ('The first thing I did was look at our monitoring dashboard'), with no self-deprecating humor or wry acknowledgment of personal foolishness.
The author lists three theories but immediately dismisses the first and jumps to heap snapshots that directly reveal the cause, with no period of genuine confusion or misreading of evidence.
The investigation goes from 'took heap snapshots' to 'noticed objects related to our caching layer' to the root cause in a single short section with no incremental clue-building.
The root cause is presented immediately after the first real diagnostic step ('Looking at the heap snapshots, I noticed...'), with no sustained tension preceding it.
No emotional states are described at any point in the investigation — no frustration, surprise, relief, or any other feeling is mentioned.
Takeaways are generic principles like 'Always monitor your memory usage' and 'Be careful with in-memory caches' rather than specific behavior changes the author now follows.
The post leads with 'Always monitor your memory usage' as its first takeaway — exactly the kind of obvious advice the rubric says should be omitted or explicitly moved past.
Takeaways like 'Heap snapshots are your friend' and 'Keep your debugging tools ready' are stated as general advice without connecting to specific narrative moments or turning points.
The framing is instructional and lecturing ('Learn to use this tool before you need it,' 'The key is to not panic'), treating the reader as someone who needs basic guidance.
There are exactly two code snippets — the problematic code and the fix — each focused and earning its place in the narrative.
Neither snippet contains inline comments pointing to the critical lines; the only annotation is a generic '// 1 hour' and '// Clean every 5 minutes' which describe values, not the bug or fix logic.
The problematic code (plain object cache with no eviction) and the fixed code (Map with TTL-based cleanup) are both shown, making the transformation visible.
Before the first snippet, the prose explains 'We had an in-memory cache that stored processed order results for deduplication purposes,' directing the reader to look at the caching logic.
No time of day, no environmental details, no Slack messages, no UI descriptions — the closest is '200MB of heap usage' and '18 hours,' which are metrics, not sensory anchors.
The draft names specific tools: Chrome DevTools, Kubernetes, Express, and Redis.
All key moments are summarized in retrospective narration ('The first thing I did was look at our monitoring dashboard,' 'I decided to take heap snapshots') rather than dramatized as scenes.
